verdicts.evidence: The logbook only parsed the paper's own Table 1 and confirmed the numbers (469/516 tasks, >140 lines, width >11, depth >8.7) match the claim; no independent re-measurement of the benchmark data was performed, and the logbook itself labels independent re-measurement as inconclusive.

The logbook parsed the paper's Table 2 and verified Claude-4-Sonnet's GM scores (36.46/32.17) and arg-max over 24 rows, but no models were independently re-run; the logbook itself states 'inconclusive (independent re-measurement).'

The logbook confirmed the three per-model numbers from Table 2, then performed a concrete count of all 24 model rows at or below 20% GM: Squirrel-Syntax shows only 10/24 (41.67%) at or below 20%, meaning most models (58.33%) actually exceed 20%, contradicting the claim's 'most evaluated LLMs failing to exceed 20%' statement for the Syntax split.

The logbook only parsed the paper's Table 1 and confirmed token counts (496.90/425.93) and function counts (21.62/17.34) match; no independent re-measurement of the benchmark scripts was performed, and the logbook itself labels independent re-measurement as inconclusive.

overall: The logbook is essentially a paper-internal verification exercise: it parses the paper's own tables and checks claims against them, without running any independent experiments or re-measuring benchmark data. The one substantive finding is a concrete arithmetic check on the paper's Table 2 showing that the 'most LLMs fail to exceed 20%' statement is false for Squirrel-Syntax, falsifying part of Claim 3.
